sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $114 billion to $184 billion [F1][F10][F177].

The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 before three straight declines of 16.5%, 1.8% and 4.6% [D153][D192][D232][D274][D316][D358].
The FY2022 peak reflected higher upstream realizations and downstream margins, which the FY2022 filing cites as the driver of a $28.0 billion rise in income before tax [P57].
The FY2025 decline came mainly from lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth as it fell 5.3% [D402][D403][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and +1.5pp of growth on a 16.5% increase [D418][D419][D420].
The FY2025 volume gain came from the Hess acquisition and higher TCO, Permian and Gulf of America production, partly offset by asset sales [P28].
Operating costs fell 3.4% while revenue fell 4.6%, so the revenue decline outran cost reduction by 1.2pp [D373][D358][D379].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% against a 30.5% net income decline because the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D361][D359][D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, a 1.6pp improvement [D338][D296].
Purchased crude oil and products decreased on lower crude and refined product prices and volumes, partly offset by higher natural gas prices and volumes [P14].
Depreciation, depletion and amortization rose to 10.7% of revenue from 8.5%, driven by higher production and higher rates [D341][D299][P12].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D345][D303].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, well above the 1.35x free-cash-flow-to-net-income ratio [F60][F20][D346][D347].
Free cash flow of $16.6 billion was an 8.8% margin, just under the 8.9% median [F80][D343][D616].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F70][D342][D348].
Operating cash flow rose on higher TCO distributions and legacy Hess contributions, which more than offset lower commodity prices [P6].
Net cash turned positive at $4.0 billion, or 2.1% of revenue, after a $156 million net debt position in FY2024 [D351][D352][D309].
Net cash as a share of revenue ranks in the 83rd percentile of six energy peers, whose median is -7.7% [D637][D638].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow, funded partly by $11.4 billion of debt issued [D353][D354][X157].
The diluted share count still rose 2.1% in FY2025, so buybacks did not offset issuance [D374].
Revenue has fallen for three straight years, from $196.9 billion in FY2023 to $184.4 billion in FY2025 [F8][F9][F10][R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 149.7% in the latest year [D270][D312][D354][R4].
The revenue basis is mixed: FY2025 is $184.4 billion in the table against $189.0 billion as first reported, so growth spanning recast and unrecast years mixes presentations [F10][X10][R3].
Non-US downstream was 34.9% of revenue and fell 13.1% in FY2025 [D517][D518][R6].
Watch net margin against the 7.9% window median; a print below it would extend the FY2025 slide from 9.2% [D613][F29][F30].
Watch free cash flow against the $16.6 billion FY2025 level and the 149.7% payout ratio; a ratio above 100% again would keep buybacks debt-funded [F80][D354].
Watch 2026 organic capex against the $18-19 billion guidance, up from $17.3 billion in FY2025 [P4][F70].
